t: Testing approaches, test plans and test data
l: Hello and welcome to Digital Tech Revision, the podcast for CCEA GCSE Digital Technology. I'm Aoife.
And I'm Conor. Today's episode is lesson D22: Testing approaches, test plans and test data.
So Conor, if someone only remembers one thing from today, what should it be?
Describe white box, black box, unit, integration and system testing. That is the heart of it.
Okay, take us through it properly.

White box testing examines the internal logic so that every path and condition is executed; it is usually done by the programmer using dry runs and trace tables. Black box testing checks inputs against expected outputs without looking at the code, usually by independent testers or users.
Makes sense. Keep going.

Unit testing checks one module on its own; integration testing checks modules work together; system testing checks the whole system against the specification. Testing is iterative, carried out repeatedly during and after development.
Right. What else do we need to know?
Use valid data (should be accepted), extreme/boundary data (at the limits), invalid data (should be rejected) and null data (nothing entered).
Time for quickfire key terms. I'll say the term, and you give me the answer the mark scheme gives credit for.
Go for it.
White box testing?
Testing the internal code, paths and logic, usually by the programmer.
Black box testing?
Testing inputs and outputs against requirements without seeing the code.
Unit testing?
Testing a single module, function or method on its own.
Integration testing?
Testing that separately built units work together.
System testing?
Testing the complete, integrated system against its specification.
Test plan?
Table listing each test, its purpose, test data, expected outcome, actual outcome and action.
